The Smooth on the Left Side of a Bar

Source: R/random_smooth.R
dot-random_smooth_lhs.Rd

Reads the left side of a bar formula and returns the smooth written there, with whether the groups also carry a random level, or NULL where the left side holds no s() or te() call.

Usage

.random_smooth_lhs(within, env)

Arguments

within

The left side of the bar, a language object.

env

The formula's environment.

Value

NULL, or a list with term, the unbuilt SmoothTerm(), and intercept, a single logical.

Details

The left side is split on +. A smooth random effect holds exactly one s() or te() call, optionally beside 1, 0 or -1, which follow the intercept convention of a model formula. Any other covariate beside the smooth signals an error naming the spelling that writes it as a term of its own.

The call is evaluated with this package's s() and te() in place of whatever the formula's environment binds to those names, so that a session with mgcv attached builds the same term.

The smooth may not carry a by variable, a sparse setting, held hyperparameters or an id. The grouping is the variable after the bar, and the hyperparameters belong to the random effect, where hyper and id of random() name them.
